lessons.title: Rolling withered leaf
lessons.html:
Why we roll the leaf

After withering, the soft leaf is rolled or cut. Rolling twists the leaf and breaks the cells inside it. The juice inside the leaf comes out onto the surface and mixes with the air. This starts fermentation, the change that turns green leaf into black tea with its colour and strong taste.

Two ways of rolling

MethodHow it worksTea it makes
Orthodox rollerA table moves in circles under a heavy box of leaf. The leaf is twisted.Long, twisted leaf grades
CTC (crush, tear, curl)Leaf goes between rollers with sharp teeth.Small, round granules, often for tea bags

Many factories first pass leaf through a rotorvane, which cuts and presses the leaf before CTC.

Getting ready

  • Check that the machine is clean. Old fermented leaf left in the machine spoils new tea.
  • Check that all guards are on.
  • Ask your supervisor for the settings: how much leaf per load, how long to roll, how much pressure.
  • Wear your overall, hair cover and boots. Remove rings and loose bracelets.

Rolling steps

  1. Load the right amount of withered leaf. Too much leaf rolls badly; too little wastes time.
  2. Start the machine as you were trained.
  3. Roll for the set time and add pressure as the supervisor says.
  4. Unload the rolled leaf. On orthodox lines, the leaf goes to a sifter (roll breaker) that breaks lumps and separates fine leaf.

Safety at the rollers

  • Never put your hand into a moving roller or CTC machine. Teeth and rollers can cut off fingers.
  • Use the stop button and lock out before clearing a blockage or cleaning.
  • Keep loose clothes and long hair tied back.
  • Rolling makes heat and noise. Wear hearing protection if the area is loud.

lessons.title: Fermenting and checking the leaf
lessons.html:
What fermentation is

In tea, "fermentation" means the leaf juice reacts with oxygen from the air. It is really oxidation. The leaf changes colour from green to a bright copper brown, and the smell changes from grassy to a sweet, fruity smell.

How fermentation is done

The rolled leaf is spread out on clean trays, floors or a moving fermenting belt (continuous fermenting machine). Cool, damp air is blown over or through it. Your supervisor gives you the depth to spread and the time.

  • Spread the leaf evenly to the right depth. Thick patches get hot and ferment too much.
  • Keep the air cool and damp. Humidifiers or wet sacks may be used.
  • Keep the area very clean. Old leaf on trays brings bacteria and sour smells.

Checking the leaf

Check the leaf often during fermentation:

CheckGoodProblem
ColourBright, even copperStill green (under), dark dull brown (over)
SmellFresh, fruity, sweetGrassy (under), sour or flat (over)
TemperatureCoolWarm to hot patches

Use a thermometer to check the leaf temperature as you were shown. Write it down.

Ending fermentation

When the leaf reaches the right colour and smell, the supervisor will say it is ready. It must go straight to the dryer. The dryer stops fermentation with heat. Leaf that waits too long over-ferments, and the tea becomes dull and flat. That tea is worth less money.

Records and cleaning

  • Record the batch, the time rolling started, time fermenting started and ended, and the temperatures.
  • Clean trays, belts and floors after each batch.
  • Report any machine noise, broken belts or humidifier problems.

Key points

  • Rolling breaks the leaf cells so the juice meets the air.
  • Never put hands into moving rollers; lock out before cleaning.
  • Spread fermenting leaf evenly and keep it cool and damp.
  • Check colour, smell and temperature often.
  • Send correctly fermented leaf straight to the dryer.
